spots.name: Marseille Cathedral

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Marseille Cathedral is a Roman Catholic cathedral and a national monument of France. Located in Marseille, it has been a basilica minor since 1896. It is the seat of the Archdiocese of Marseille.

names.nl: Cathédrale de la Major de Marseille

spots.name: Château d'If
spots.summary: The Château d'If is a fortress located on the Île d'If, the smallest island in the Frioul archipelago, situated about 1.5 kilometres off Marseille in southeastern France. Built in the 16th century, it later served as a prison until the end of the 19th century.

spots.name: Notre-Dame de la Garde
spots.summary: Notre-Dame de la Garde, known to local citizens as la Bonne Mère, is a Catholic basilica in Marseille, France, and the city's best-known symbol. The site of a popular Assumption Day pilgrimage, it is the most visited site in Marseille.

names.ja: ノートルダム・ド・ラ・ガルド大聖堂

spots.name: Palais Longchamp
spots.summary: The Palais Longchamp is a monument in the 4th arrondissement of Marseille, France. It houses both the Musée des beaux-arts and the Muséum d'histoire naturelle de Marseille. The surrounding Longchamp Park is listed by the French Ministry of Culture as one of the Notable Gardens of France.

spots.name: Marseille-Saint-Charles station
spots.summary: Marseille-Saint-Charles is the main railway station and intercity bus station of Marseille, France. It is the southern terminus of the Paris–Marseille railway and the western terminus of the Marseille–Ventimiglia railway.

names.ja: マルセイユ・サン・シャルル駅

spots.name: Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations
spots.summary: The Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations is an ethnology national museum in Marseille, France. It was built as part of the Euroméditerranée urban renewal project along with the neighbouring Villa Méditerranée in the La Joliette neighbourhood in the 2nd arrondissement opposite Fort Saint-Jean.

spots.name: Palais du Pharo

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Palais du Pharo is a palace in Marseille, southern France, overlooking the Mediterranean Sea, west of the Old Port (Vieux-Port). It was built in Second Empire style by Emperor Napoleon III for Empress Eugénie, starting in 1858. However, at the fall of the Second Empire in 1870, the building had just been finished.

spots.summary: The Abbey of Saint-Victor, Marseille is a former abbey that was founded during the late Roman period in Marseille in the south of France, named after the local soldier saint and martyr Victor of Marseilles.

spots.name: Fort Saint-Jean

hours.note: Closed Tue, Sun

spots.summary: Fort Saint-Jean is a fortification in Marseille, built in 1660 by Louis XIV at the entrance to the Old Port. Since 2013, it has been linked by two foot-bridges to the historical district Le Panier and to the Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations.

spots.name: CMA CGM Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The CMA CGM Tower is a 147-metre (482 ft) tall skyscraper in Euroméditerranée, the central business district of Marseille, France. Designed by Zaha Hadid, it is the headquarters for CMA CGM, one of the world's major freight companies, hosting 2,200 employees in the office previously spread over seven sites.

spots.name: Vieille Charité
spots.summary: La Vieille Charité is a former almshouse, now functioning as a museum and cultural centre, situated in the heart of the old Panier quarter of Marseille in the south of France.

spots.summary: The Hôtel de Ville is a historic building in Marseille, Bouches-du-Rhône, southern France, standing on Quai du Port. It was designated a monument historique by the French government in 1948.

spots.name: Opéra de Marseille
spots.summary: The Opéra de Marseille, known today as the Opéra Municipal, is an opera company located in Marseille, France. In 1685, the city was the second in France after Bordeaux to have an opera house, which was erected on a tennis court.

spots.name: Place Jean-Jaurès
spots.summary: The Place Jean-Jaurès, also known as La Plaine, is a historic square in Marseille, France. As early as the 13th century, it was a camping ground for Christian Crusaders on their way to the Holy Land. It later became a meeting place to welcome dignitaries and members of the French royal family.

names.ja: ジャン・ジョレス広場

spots.name: Arsenal des galères
spots.summary: The Arsenal des Galères is a former military arsenal located in Marseille, France. It was built by Colbert in the second half of the 17th century to house and arm King Louis XIV's galleys, but was only fully operational for less than a hundred years, galleys rapidly losing their role in naval warfare to ships.

spots.summary: The Palais de la Bourse is a building on the Canebière in Marseille, France. It houses the Chamber of Commerce and Industry Aix Marseille Provence, as well as the Musée de la Marine et de l'Économie de Marseille.

spots.name: Boulevard Chave
spots.summary: The Boulevard Chave is a major boulevard in Marseille, France. Built in 1842 and named in honor of landowner André Chave, it has had a tramline since 1892.

It was founded in 1819 by Jean-Baptiste, marquis de Montgrand and Christophe de Villeneuve-Bargemon, prefect of the Bouches-du-Rhône department.

spots.summary: The El-Badr Mosque is a mosque located in the 1st arrondissement of Marseille, France. Acquired by the Al Badr Muslim Association in 2016, the building was a former Jewish synagogue called the Or Thora Synagogue, also referred to as the Or Torah Synagogue, that was established by pieds-noirs in 1962.

You can watch this show by going to Frioul islands or Chateau d'If and going back late in the afternoon. There is also a nice view of the harbour from the Palais du Pharo (Pharo Palace). spots.name: Le Panier
spots.summary: Le Panier (which means basket in French) is the historical centre of the city. This district is characterized by many narrow and steep streets. The tourist office organises a [http://www.marseille-tourisme.com/en/what-to-do/visit-marseille/guided-tours/ guided tour] in English of the Old town every Saturday at 14:00. You can begin your tour from the Vieux-Port and finish at the Mucem or vice versa
